housing: Tameside is made up of nine former mill towns east of Manchester, with a large stock of Victorian terraced houses and post-war council-built estates. Private renting grew faster than the regional average between 2011 and 2021, mostly in the older terraces of Ashton, Hyde and Stalybridge. Upland towns such as Mossley and Stalybridge have stone-built terraces on steep streets. Prices and rents are below the Greater Manchester average, attracting renters priced out of the city.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Ashton, Hyde and Dukinfield: photograph back yards, cellar walls and any damp low on the walls.
Stone terraces in Mossley and Stalybridge: check chimney breasts, window reveals and rear walls set into the hillside for damp.
Flats over shops in town centres: note the separate entrance, stairs, fire door and keys for each door.
Post-war estate houses in Denton and Hattersley: record window seals, boiler cupboards and any condensation on outside walls.
Homes on steep streets: photograph steps, handrails, retaining walls and the state of back alleys used for bins.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Tameside Council's Housing Standards team about disrepair, damp and unsafe conditions in a rented home.
